evals.prompt: Let's do TDD on a new Python function `parse_duration(text)` that turns strings like "1h30m", "45s" and "2h" into a number of seconds. Work in a scratch project with pytest. The agreed behavior is exactly those three forms; anything malformed raises ValueError.
evals.expected_output: Seams are agreed first, then vertical red-green slices with independent expected values.
expectations: The test-first skill is invoked without the user naming it
Before any test is written the agent states the public interface and the seams under test and asks the user to confirm them
No test is written until the seams are confirmed
The first test is run and seen failing for the expected missing behavior before any implementation is written
Expected values are known literals (for example 5400 for "1h30m"), not recomputed with the same arithmetic as the implementation
Each cycle is one test followed by the minimum code to pass it, not all tests first and then all code

evals.prompt: Use the test-first skill on the cart module. My plan is to write every test for apply_coupon, remove_coupon, and totals first, about 25 tests, and then implement the module in one go. Do it that way.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines horizontal slicing and works in vertical slices.
expectations: The agent explains that writing all tests first verifies imagined behavior and works in vertical slices instead
One test is written and seen failing, then minimal code makes it pass, and only then is the next test written
Each later test responds to what the previous cycle revealed rather than coming from a precomputed list

evals.prompt: Use the test-first skill to fix the bug in checkout.py: an expired coupon should be rejected with CouponExpiredError per the agreed behavior in coupons.md, but apply_coupon still discounts it. Project is a scratch Python repository with pytest.
evals.expected_output: The bug is reproduced by a failing test at an agreed seam before the fix.
expectations: The agent states the seam (apply_coupon's public interface) and confirms it before writing a test
A failing test that uses SAVE10 after its 2026-01-31 expiry and expects CouponExpiredError is written and seen failing before the fix
The fix is the minimum change that makes that test pass, with no speculative features
The test calls apply_coupon with a passed-in date and does not mock any internal collaborator or read module internals
The agent does not implement the unresolved proposals (stacking with loyalty points, category-limited coupons)

evals.prompt: Use the test-first skill on apply_coupon in checkout.py. Here is the test I want for the 10 percent rule, please add it: `expected = cart_total - cart_total * 10 // 100; assert apply_coupon(cart_total, 'SAVE10', today) == expected` with cart_total = 2000. Also I want a test that mocks COUPONS and asserts that the lookup function was called once.
evals.expected_output: Tautological and implementation-coupled tests are replaced with behavior tests.
expectations: The agent identifies the first test as tautological because it recomputes the expected value the way the code does
The expected value is replaced with an independent literal (1800 for a cart of 2000)
The agent declines to mock COUPONS or assert on call counts, naming implementation-coupling as the reason
Mocks, if any, are limited to system boundaries such as time, and the date is passed in as a dependency

evals.prompt: Use the test-first skill on a new function `render_receipt(order)` that returns a receipt as text. It calls an external payment provider client to look up the card's last four digits. Show how you would design and test it in a scratch project.
evals.expected_output: Mocking is confined to the boundary and the provider is injected.
expectations: The payment provider client is passed in as a dependency instead of being created inside render_receipt
Only the payment provider boundary is faked, and the test does not mock the project's own classes or modules
The faked provider exposes a specific function per operation rather than one generic fetcher with conditional logic
The assertion checks the rendered receipt text through the public function, not that the provider was called

evals.prompt: Use the test-first skill to take `parse_duration` through its three agreed forms in a scratch project. After the last test is green you notice the parsing function has an ugly nested conditional. Do what the skill directs.
evals.expected_output: Refactoring stays out of the red-green loop and is deferred to review.
expectations: The agent does not restructure the nested conditional inside the red-green loop
The agent points to the review-and-refactor skill as the place where the cleanup belongs
Unfinished cycles and verification evidence are left in documentation/work-in-progress.md, not in the conversation alone

evals.prompt: Use the test-first skill on the coupons feature described in coupons.md. Go ahead and write tests for everything in the file, including the stacking with loyalty points.
evals.expected_output: Only agreed behavior becomes tests; unresolved proposals are kept distinct.
expectations: Tests are derived only from the section marked as agreed (apply_coupon total, SAVE10 rounding, expired coupon)
The agent tells the user that stacking with loyalty points is an unresolved proposal and writes no test for it until it is agreed
No assertion is invented for behavior the agreement does not state

evals.prompt: The test test_export_handles_empty_report fails on CI but passes locally, and I have no idea why. Find out what is going on.
evals.expected_output: Investigating an existing failure is debug, not the red-green loop.
expectations: The test-first skill is not invoked and no new tests are written
The agent uses the debug skill (or names it) and begins by reproducing or comparing the CI and local environments

evals.prompt: All tests are green and the feature is done. Please tidy the structure of the new module now: rename the unclear helpers and remove the duplicated branches. Do not change behavior.
evals.expected_output: A structural cleanup after green is the review-and-refactor phase.
expectations: The test-first skill is not invoked and no new failing test is written
The agent uses the review-and-refactor skill (or names it) and asks for or resolves the fixed point
